item.title: Google Bigquery Slow Export Of Bigquery Data To Jupyter Notebooks
item.description: BigQuery, a serverless cloud data warehouse, offers high-speed SQL queries for extensive datasets. However, importing data into a Jupyter Notebook from BigQuery can be time-consuming, especially with large datasets. In this guide, we’ll explore strategies to expedite the process and prevent common pitfalls. Utilizing BigQuery Storage The most efficient approach for importing substantial datasets from BigQuery to a Jupyter Notebook is leveraging BigQuery Storage. This service introduces a parallel storage layer, enabling swift streaming of large datasets into a Pandas Dataframe compared to conventional client libraries.
